text:
sam: Can we build a small, focused dashboard for continuous-batching tuning? I want: batch headroom, queue depth by priority, token/sec by model family, KV-cache miss rate, and a kernel-selection mismatch signal. Perf regressions last week surfaced some hidden pressure patterns.

lia: +1. Minimal set of panels first. My suggested panels: 
- Batch headroom (capacity - inflight tokens) pct
- Queue depth histogram (by age bucket)
- Token/s per model and per route
- KV cache miss rate and miss latency P95
- Kernel-mismatch rate (requests routed to fallback kernels)
- Microbatch formation latency (time from enqueue -> batch start)

jonas: Also add a panel for "soft budget" violations, i.e., when per-request token budget is exceeded and batcher had to split. That correlates with more KV misses.

lia: Example PromQL sketches (feel free to refine):
```promql
# token/sec by model
sum(rate(tokens_emitted_total{job="batcher"}[1m])) by (model)

# batch headroom pct
(sum(batch_capacity_tokens{job="batcher"}) - sum(batch_inflight_tokens{job="batcher"})) / sum(batch_capacity_tokens{job="batcher"})

# KV cache miss rate
sum(rate(kvcache_miss_total{job="batcher"}[5m])) / sum(rate(kvcache_request_total{job="batcher"}[5m]))

# microbatch formation latency p95
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(batch_formation_duration_seconds_bucket{job="batcher"}[5m])) by (le))
```

anna: For alerts, I propose: 
- Batch headroom < 10% for >2m -> severity=high
- KV cache miss rate > 20% for >5m -> severity=medium
- Kernel-mismatch rate > 5% for >10m -> severity=low (investigate slow rollouts)

jonas: How do we sample traces for microbatch formation? We shouldn't trace every request. Suggest sampling 1% by default, increase to 10% when headroom < 5% or queue depth > 80th pct.

sam: That sampling rule sounds good. Lia, can you drop a draft dashboard JSON we can iterate on? Keep panels small and numeric first, then add graphs. Use short titles: Headroom pct, Queue depth (age buckets), Tokens/s (model), KV miss %, Kernel fallback %.

lia: Will do. I'll also add a "batcher health" composite panel that computes a simple score: 0-100 combining headroom, KV miss, kernel mismatch, and microbatch latency. Score formula in the panel notes.

infra-bot: deploy-batcher-monitoring: new grafana-dash "batcher-headroom-health" pushed to staging (sha: a1b2c3). Promote with `/deploy promote grafana-batcher-headroom` when QA passes.

sam: QA checklist: 
- Verify headroom math with synthetic load (small / medium / burst)
- Confirm KV miss % matches KV service logs
- Run kernel selection A/B to validate fallback signal

jonas: I'll run synthetic profiles tomorrow morning and capture traces with the new sampling rule. Tagging @lia for dashboard follow-up. :rocket:

sam: Thanks — once in staging let's run the e2e load and check correlations. If we see repeated soft budget splits, we should tune target token budgets per model family and consider dynamic queue reshuffling.

lia: Draft dashboard will be in the staging folder by EOD. I'll paste the JSON and key panel queries in this thread when ready.

anna: One more ask: include a small table panel listing top 10 routes by token/sec and their current quantization/kernels in use (helps triage perf regressions).

sam: Perfect. That's the plan. We'll iterate after the first run.
